messages:
Maya: Need a concise, reproducible benchmark plan for tool/function-call + JSON-mode overhead. Goal: apples-to-apples vs plain text gen and to surface retry/validation tail behavior.

Ryan: Agreed. I think we should split into microbench -> synthetic matrix -> replay. Microbench isolates JSON validator and dispatch; synthetic isolates batcher/kv/kernel; replay validates real shapes.

Sara: Constraints: pin model revision + tokenizer seed, temperature=0, same max_new_tokens, deterministic routing for tool calls, and record KV warm vs cold.

Alex: Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 token latency, e2e latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, host CPU, memory, retry counts, validation failure rate, payload sizes. Also log kernel selection and effective batch size per generation step.

Maya: Add per-request fields in traces: bench.run_id, request.shape (prompt_len, num_tool_calls), kernel_hint, batch_size_at_step, kv_hit_ratio, validation_result. Keep logs sampled to avoid huge volumes.

Ryan: Synthetic matrix proposal (example):
```
mode: synthetic
concurrency: [1,4,8,16]
pattern: toolcall-heavy; 50% tool calls per request
json_validation: [enabled, disabled]
kv_state: [cold, warm]
retry_injection: [0%, 1%]
model: mpt-inf@rev-20250512
```

Sara: For the replay harness: sample real requests but strip streaming frames and enforce deterministic seeds. Respect original inter-arrival shapes for request shape but throttle to target QPS so batcher behavior emerges.

Alex: Important microbench: run validator in-process across payload sizes (1KB, 10KB, 50KB) and in two modes: single-threaded vs worker-pool. Measure latency, CPU, and any lock contention.

perf-bot: FYI: prior runs showed ~10-14% p95 overhead with validation on; suspected CPU-bound parser and occasional host GC/stop-the-world spikes when validation runs inline.

Maya: If validator is CPU-heavy, experiment with offloading to a small worker pool (size = cpu_count/2) and measure added queueing latency. Also test isolating validator on separate cores (taskset) to see if host GC/CPU scheduling is the root cause.

Ryan: Retry modeling: inject a small fraction (1%) of validation errors or transient tool-fail responses. Runtime should retry up to 2x with exponential backoff. Measure duplicate token output, how retries affect batch packing, and if KV cache entries are invalidated.

Sara: Also capture batcher-level metrics: average batch size, batch size distribution, number of batches per second, and any backpressure signals when validator queue fills.

Alex: Kernel selection logs: record chosen kernel id, reason (e.g., aten_fused, cuda_fastpath), and estimated FLOPs. Will help correlate kernel choices with latency deltas in JSON vs plain text.

Maya: Run ordering: 1) validator microbench; 2) synthetic matrix (across concurrencies and kv states); 3) replay runs (3 different production days sampled); 4) collate deltas vs baseline (no validation, no retries).

Ryan: Implementation notes for replay change: add deterministic seed option, strip streaming metadata, add --inject-retry-rate N flag, and ensure harness logs original timing shape for analysis.

perf-bot: Starting microbench: run_id=1761112223-a1, validator-only across two host types (c6gn-like and c7a-like) and two interpreter modes (inline vs worker-pool). Expect ~30m.

Sara: Collation: output CSV rows per scenario with fields: run_id, model_rev, concurrency, kv_state, json_validation, retry_rate, p50_tok_ms, p95_tok_ms, p99_tok_ms, e2e_p95_ms, tokens_per_sec, gpu_util, cpu_user_pct, validation_fail_rate, retry_count. Provide a small notebook that consumes the CSV and plots the deltas vs baseline.

Maya: I'll own collation and notebook. Please attach raw trace bundles (jaeger/zipkin) and kernel-selection logs to the run artifact. Also please add exact command lines used for each run in the artifact so infra can reproduce.

Alex: One more thing 609: for synthetic tool calls, ensure deterministic tool behavior (no external network) and a tiny compute-bound mock tool so we measure runtime behavior not downstream variance.

Ryan: I'll patch the harness to include a local mock tool that returns structured JSON and a small compute delay (5-20ms) so tool latency appears realistic.

Maya: Acceptance criteria for initial experiment: 1) microbench results for validator across sizes and pool modes; 2) synthetic matrix completed with CSV; 3) one replay day analyzed; 4) quick regression check vs baseline showing clear numbers for p95 overhead when validation enabled and when retry injection enabled.

Sara: Also add a short incident-like blurb if any scenario shows >20% p95 regression or retry amplification >2x, so we can triage separately.

Maya: Thanks all. Aim to have first artifacts within 48 hours. Tag me on PRs and upload run artifacts to the bench bucket with path `bench/1761112223/`. :rocket:
